problem.text: Safetensors metadata exposed only a stringified Torch dtype, not the dtype object returned by convert_dtype.

reasoning.text: The change separates runtime metadata from JSON-ready metadata: list_tensors retains the existing dtype string and optionally adds torch_dtype. The quantization inventory explicitly opts out of the object-valued field before JSON serialization.

impact.text: Existing calls receive richer metadata by default; quantization_config.json retains its previous tensor-record fields. Tensor loading and its dtype conversions are unchanged.

source_notes.text: The earlier inventory entry establishes that list_tensors and the sidecar exporter were introduced together, using header metadata rather than loading tensor payloads.

Issue #33, “Error converting model,” reports file-opening failures and later GLM sampling trouble. Issue #38, “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” reports a padding/sliced-layer size mismatch. Their relationship to this task is only an inferred shared-loader context: neither discussion establishes a motivation for retaining dtype objects.

limitations: No repository implementation, Torch dtype serialization, tensor loading or end-to-end conversion was executed. The bounded Python check modeled the new dictionary branch using a nonserializable sentinel.
Whole-parent-tree literal searches establish the inspected in-repository callers, not dynamic or external consumers.

chapters.title: Retain native dtype objects without changing exported metadata

claims.text: list_tensors still selects an exact prefix or dot-delimited descendants, requires new_tensors to be None, and derives shape and payload byte count from cached headers. convert_dtype supplies the native Torch dtype; the new torch_dtype field stores that object without replacing the existing dtype string. only_serializable defaults to False and suppresses only the new field when true.

The exporter change supplies a necessary companion to the richer default. create_quantization_config_json places each listing under stored_tensors, eventually passed to json.dumps; its new only_serializable=True argument preserves the prior record structure instead of exporting native objects.

Whole-tree searches found one list_tensors definition and three caller functions. The exporter opts out. Gemma3VisionModel.get_additional_compiled_tensors and the corresponding Mistral3 method retain their old calls, so both now return the additional field. Their inspected consumer, compile_model, reads n_bytes for shard allocation and then loads tensors by key; it neither serializes these metadata dictionaries nor consumes torch_dtype. These paths therefore tolerate the added field without requiring it.

A standard-library transcription verified object identity retention, equality of the remaining record fields, and JSON round-tripping of the serializable branch. The object-bearing sentinel branch raised TypeError; this models the serialization boundary rather than testing Torch or the repository implementation.

annotation.summary: Adds native Torch dtype objects to Safetensors listings by default, while explicitly preserving JSON-ready listings for quantization metadata export.
